title: ElmNET: A Europe-wide Dendroecological Network for Ulmus laevis Pall.
text:
Project
This ILTER-funded project establishes a Europe-wide tree-ring network for Ulmus laevis to advance dendroecological research and strengthen the evidence base for monitoring, conservation, and forest management.
ElmNET will provide a harmonized dataset for assessing growth, vitality, and climate sensitivity across the species’ distribution range.

title: ElmNET: A Europe-wide Dendroecological Network for Ulmus laevis Pall.
text:
Background
Despite its wide distribution and ecological importance, Ulmus laevis remains poorly represented in dendroecological research, forest monitoring, and forest management. Unlike Ulmus glabra and Ulmus minor, which have been severely affected by Dutch elm disease, U. laevis appears comparatively resilient. However, evidence across its full distribution range is still limited.
The species occurs across a remarkably broad ecological gradient, including swamp forests and forested peatlands, riparian forests exposed to fluctuating water levels and periodic flooding, and comparatively dry forests with mineral soils, and wastelands.
Comparing tree-ring records from these contrasting environments will improve our understanding of how growth responds to climatic extremes, changing hydrological conditions, and other environmental pressures. It will also help determine whether these responses differ among regions, habitats, and populations.

title: ElmNET: A Europe-wide Dendroecological Network for Ulmus laevis Pall.
Participation
text:
We actively welcome collaboration with researchers, institutions, and tree-ring laboratories throughout the distribution range of Ulmus laevis.
Contributions may consist of previously measured tree-ring series or newly collected increment cores. Sites from underrepresented regions and environmentally unusual locations, particularly dry sites, are especially valuable for the network.
At least 15 sampled trees per site are required, ideally accompanied by metadata and stand information.
Researchers interested in contributing data or sampling additional sites are invited to contact the project coordinator.
